transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Clearview Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Eng Manager), Lena Cho (Security)

Summary/Topics (auto): Hosted API walkthrough, streaming demo, model params, retry/backoff behavior, security questions (SOC2/KMS), pilot plan.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, i'll run through a quick hosted API demo with Ethan and then we'll leave time for questions, is that still the plan?
[00:12] Maya: Yep sounds great, thanks Samira. We have about 45 minutes. Carlos will jump in on infra stuff and Lena on security.
[00:20] Samira: Perfect. Quick agenda: 1) what Clearview is trying to build, 2) demo of chat/text generation endpoints including streaming and params, 3) retry semantics and best practices, 4) Q&A and next steps.
[00:35] Ethan: I'll kick off the demo; i'll share my screen — showing a notebook calling the hosted API. Note the endpoint is a simple POST to /v1/generate, we support chat and text, structured tool-calls etc.
[01:05] Ethan: (typing) First call: synchronous response for a short prompt. We set temperature 0.2, max_tokens 150. Response returns tokens + metadata (model, request_id, latency_ms).
[01:30] Carlos: Quick question on tokens: how do you measure token pricing vs characters, we have long messages from customers.
[01:40] Samira: Pricing is per-token for generation and embeddings; we provide token counters in the SDK and console so you can estimate. For long prompts we recommend prefix caching or summarization to cut prompt size.
[02:10] Ethan: Now switching to streaming. I change the request to stream=true and show a live stream of partial tokens back to the client. This reduces perceived latency for users.
[02:35] Ethan: Note that streaming is chunked deltas — you get partial text as it's generated and then a final event. We surface event types: token, done, error.
[03:05] Maya: That streaming looked snappy, what does that do to throughput/cost?
[03:15] Ethan: Streaming doesn't change per-token compute cost, but it improves UX — you can start rendering sooner. For throughput we batch on the server side where possible; batching and KV cache can reduce per-token cost for repeated prefixes.
[03:45] Carlos: Any special client libraries for handling reconnects? We have flaky mobile connections.
[03:55] Ethan: Good question — we recommend using the SDK which handles automatic reconnects and incremental resume where feasible. For mobile we also suggest small chunking windows and idempotency keys for upstream requests so retries are safe.
[04:20] Lena: On retries — is there an idempotency token or request id we can set? We need to make sure duplicates won't double-charge.
[04:35] Samira: Yes, we accept idempotency keys on write calls. The platform will dedupe within a bounded window. We also return request_id in the response for reconciliation.
[04:50] Ethan: For retry policy we recommend exponential backoff with jitter; typical client pattern: try up to 3 retries for transient 5xx or 429 with increasing backoff. We also show rate-limit headers in responses so you can adapt.
[05:20] Maya: Can you show param controls that affect quality vs cost — like temperature and top_p?
[05:30] Ethan: Sure. Temperature increased to 0.9 makes outputs more creative; lower values more deterministic. top_p tunes nucleus sampling. max_tokens caps output length and is a major lever on cost. We demo an example with temperature 0.9 -> longer, more varied response, and with 0.2 -> concise, conservative response.
[06:10] Carlos: Do you provide automated suggestions for settings? We saw mention of Redwood Optimize...
[06:20] Samira: Yes, Redwood Optimize will analyze traffic patterns and suggest batching, quantization, and parameter choices for cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll include a sample Optimize report in the pilot.
[06:40] Ethan: Back to streaming — I'm showing a demo of a chat UI with streaming. The client receives token events and appends them. We log partial latencies per token to the console.
[07:10] (short pause, Ethan clicks)
[07:25] Maya: Can we do function/tool calling and structured JSON in hosted API? Our app calls downstream services.
[07:35] Ethan: Yes, Redwood supports structured output and function/tool calling patterns. We map to JSON schemas and can validate outputs; this helps ensure predictable downstream handling.
[08:05] Lena: Security: we need SOC 2, customer-managed keys, and audit logs. Do you support KMS integration and VPC endpoints?
[08:18] Samira: We do. Hosted customers can integrate with KMS for key wrapping; for higher compliance we offer Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) but hosted can integrate with customer-managed KMS in many cases. We also produce audit logs, request traces, and long-term retention options if needed.
[08:50] Lena: For hosted, can you guarantee data is not used to train models?
[08:58] Samira: Yes we provide a contractual assurance for enterprise customers that data will not be used for model training, and we have options to disable logging of content. We'll send the security whitepaper and contract language.
[09:20] Maya: On latency: we care about 95th percentile under 300ms for short prompts. How do you achieve that?
[09:30] Ethan: We have optimized serving runtime, continuous batching, and region-aware routing. For sub-300ms you can pin to a low-latency instance, use smaller model variants, and enable streaming for perceived latency. We'll run a small benchmark during the POC to validate.
[10:00] Carlos: Is there a way to route by policy — like prefer lower cost region but fail to low-latency region if required?
[10:08] Samira: Yes, Smart routing supports policy-based routing (latency, cost, region, tier) with automated fallbacks. We can show config examples in the console.
[10:30] Ethan: Now i want to demo retries and error handling. I'll simulate a transient server error; the SDK returns 502, we retry with backoff, SDK logs indicate attempt counts, and eventual success.
[11:00] Ethan: I also show how to use idempotency keys in the payload: X-Idempotency-Key header or 'idempotency_key' field. If a success already recorded, server returns 200 and indicates deduped=true.
[11:25] Maya: What about rate limits for bursty traffic? We expect traffic spikes from promotional events.
[11:35] Samira: We have per-account quotas and burst tokens; Dedicated customers can get predictable throughput. For hosted we provide burst capacity tiers and can pre-warm. We'll include options in the pilot pricing.
[12:00] (Ethan scrolls)
[12:15] Ethan: Switching to the Console — here's the per-route model dashboard: request per second, token breakdown, cost estimation. You can drill into per-token latency slices and sample traces.
[12:45] Carlos: Nice to have trace-level debugging. Does the console let us create canary rollouts by model version?
[12:55] Samira: Yes, rollout controls allow canary percent, automatic rollback on error rate/latency regressions, and A/B testing.
[13:20] Maya: For the pilot, we'll likely start with hosted and evaluate Dedicated if throughput/cost needs rise.
[13:30] Samira: That's a common path. Start hosted pilot, validate latency and cost, then move to Dedicated if needed. We'll include a migration checklist.
[13:45] Lena: For compliance we need a data processing addendum and encryption at rest.
[13:55] Samira: We'll attach the DPA and encryption docs; hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit. For additional controls we can propose Private deployment.
[14:10] Ethan: Quick note on prompt caching/KV cache: if you have repeated prefixes (e.g., user instructions), the runtime can reuse KV cache to reduce compute. That particularly helps long context workloads.
[14:35] Maya: For our use-case we do lots of personalization per user so not sure how much prefix reuse we'll get.
[14:45] Ethan: Understood; Optimize can still recommend quantization and batching strategies tailored to your traffic profile.
[15:05] (Silence as Ethan flips slides)
[15:20] Samira: Any questions on pricing? We'll propose a pilot package: three months, limited tokens with X% discount and up to N streaming connections.
[15:35] Carlos: We'd like an estimate for 1M tokens/month and streaming concurrency of ~50.
[15:45] Samira: I'll include a concrete quote in the follow-up.
[16:00] Maya: One more technical deep dive: how do you expose model metrics for quality monitoring?
[16:08] Ethan: We support custom evals bound to prompt sets, continuous quality monitoring, and regression alerts tied to specific prompts. The console can run evals regularly against new model versions.
[16:35] Lena: We'll need to see the SOC2 cert and vulnerability assessment.
[16:42] Samira: We'll send SOC2 and pen-test summaries in the follow-up.
[16:50] Samira: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: Samira to send pricing + pilot proposal, Ethan to share benchmark checklist and test harness repo link, Redwood to send SOC2 and KMS docs, customer to provide data residency/PII constraints.
[17:10] Maya: Thanks all, that was helpful. We'll aim to review materials early next week.
[17:18] Samira: Great, thanks everyone. Bye.

References shared during call: https://redwood.ai/security (security whitepaper), https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-api (API docs), demo notebook link: link to gist (not included).
